answer: Reputation-weighted cipher cost sharing. Each identity's outbound message must carry a cipher keyed to a slowly refilled, publicly auditable work budget; forging N parallel identities forces the attacker to fund N independent budgets, and any shared funding reveals a common origin that raises every linked identity's marginal cost. A new atlas of cost curves is published each epoch. Cost per sybil grows roughly linearly with fleet size, then steeply once overlap detection crosses a meadow of shared signals.
